sources.decision: SQL and relational expressions can access capabilities; settings are defense in depth, not a sandbox.
Native extensions carry process privileges; unsigned/custom repository decisions require explicit trust.
Native settings export via duckdb_settings; explicit resource settings.
Choose embedded single-process ownership versus supported Quack access; do not generalize old multi-process limitations to all 2.0 modes.
Buffer-manager limit is not whole-process memory isolation.
Projection/filter pushdown, row-group layout and partitioning need workload measurements.
Concurrent resource competition motivates explicit budgets; historical connection/process descriptions are version-qualified.
Parquet staging and parallel output are candidates to measure, not promised universal speedups.
Hypothetical/AI-assisted article is explicitly low authority; its memory/spill concerns are checked against official documentation.
Client/server parallelism and execution placement motivate separate measurement. Reported ratios are not generalized to 2.0 workloads.
Alpha benchmark is version/workload specific. No guaranteed speedup, global CLI replacement or curl-to-shell installer is imported.
Engine-author explanation supports managed-memory versus process-memory distinction.
Verify eligible formats and actual execution path; do not promise async I/O benefits for every format based on an alpha benchmark.
